anchor.quote: This is not unique to the Agnicayana. The same engineered-obsolescence principle appears in other ritual technologies. The Tibetan sand mandala is constructed with painstaking precision over days or weeks, then deliberately destroyed: the sand is swept into a single mound and poured into running water. The mandala that did its work correctly is dismantled because the dismantlement is the work's completion, not its failure. The Ganesh visarjana immerses the painstakingly-crafted clay murti into the sea at the festival's end. The Christian Lent ashes are made from the previous year's blessed palms. In each case, the sacred object is engineered to dissolve at its cycle's term, and its dissolution is what marks the operation's success.
